evidence.text: The scanned 菜 entry reads: “形声字。从艸，采声。本义是指蔬菜。” It quotes Shuowen, “菜，艸之可食者”; cites 《尔雅·广物》“菜谓之蔬” and 《论语·乡党》“虽疏食菜羹，瓜祭，必齐如也”; and says the character also refers to dishes collectively, with 荤菜、川菜 and a 《北史·胡叟传》 example. The entry’s headword, cited characters, component clause, and prose were checked against the supplied scan pixels. It ends before the following 薄 entry. Page 62 was also inspected; it is a separate page and does not continue 菜.
evidence.title: 《字源》 (2012 edition record; catalogue metadata only)

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 菜 entry; 形義通解 and cited historical uses
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 菜 as 艸 plus phonetic 采, with vegetables as its basic meaning. It reports bronze forms used as a place name, Qin slips writing the vegetable word as 采 in 采(菜)羹, and cites the Guoyu sentence “庶人食菜，祀以魚.” It also cites a 《北史·胡叟傳》 example for use as a collective term for dishes. These are the database’s reports; its headword page alone does not give a date or specimen provenance for the bronze examples.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 菜

evidence.source: 許慎《說文解字》 as transcribed in CUHK Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.field: 菜 entry; graphic analysis and gloss
evidence.text: The entry reproduces the Shuowen definition “艸之可食者。从艸，采聲”: edible plants; from 艸, with 采 supplying the sound. This is an early explicit structural account, not independent proof of every detail of 菜’s earlier graphic history.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 菜

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 采 entry; independent component graphic history
evidence.text: The database’s analysis of 采 describes oracle-bone forms as a hand above 木 or 果, interpreted as picking fruit from a tree. It gives the picking sense and discusses the relationship of 采 and 採. This bears on 采’s own history; it does not by itself establish a derivation of the word 菜 from the verb ‘gather, pluck.’
evidence.title: 漢語甲骨部件分析 — 爪

evidence.source: Wiktionary, 菜 entry, citing named reconstruction systems
evidence.field: Zhengzhang Old Chinese; phonetic component; Middle Chinese and modern reflexes
evidence.text: The opened entry identifies 采 as the phonetic component for 菜 in Zhengzhang Shangfang’s system (2003), giving 菜 *sʰɯːs and 采 *sʰɯːʔ, with a shared onset and rhyme and a difference in final *-s. It separately gives Baxter–Sagart 2014 forms 菜 /*s.r̥ˤəʔ-s/ and 采 /*s.r̥ˤəʔ/. These are system-specific reconstructions, not direct recordings; the page’s proposed derivation of 菜 as ‘what is gathered or plucked’ with a nominal suffix is not independently established by the phonetic analysis.
evidence.title: 菜 — Wiktionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary, 采 entry, citing Zhengzhang Shangfang and Baxter–Sagart
evidence.field: 采 modern readings and historical phonology
evidence.text: The entry gives modern Mandarin cǎi, Middle Chinese Baxter transcription tshojX, Zhengzhang Old Chinese *sʰɯːʔ, and Baxter–Sagart 2014 /*s.r̥ˤəʔ/. Paired with the separately inspected 菜 entry, the Zhengzhang readings are compatible with the reported phonetic role; modern reading similarity alone is not evidence for that role.
evidence.title: 采 — Wiktionary

evidence.text: Official Unihan record for U+83DC 菜 gives kMandarin cài. This confirms the current reading only, not an ancient sound relationship.

evidence.field: 菜; Japanese senses and dated examples
evidence.text: The dictionary records a Japanese ‘vegetable/edible plant’ example in the Man’yōshū (8th century), and a ‘side dish’ example in 今昔物語集 (c. 1120). Its word-history note describes native な usage for side dishes and later general use of the Sino-Japanese reading sai. These attestations document Japanese use and do not establish the origin of 菜’s Chinese graph.

The exact earliest secure attestation of the full 菜 graph remains unclear in the inspected references. CUHK reports bronze forms and Qin slip usage but the opened entry supplies no inscription dates or specimen particulars.

CUHK and the printed 《字源》 both report 采 as 菜’s phonetic component; neither inspected source independently establishes the proposed lexical derivation of 菜 from 采 ‘gather/pluck’ plus a nominal suffix. The derivation cited secondarily to Sagart (1999) and Schuessler (2007) was not verified in those underlying works.

Qin 采(菜)羹 is reported in specialist/database accounts, but the specific slip image and an edition transcription were not independently inspected here. The report is not a claim that this research visually read the slip.

The inspected local 《字源》 OCR matches the scan in the 菜 headword prose. Neighboring 蔫 OCR includes suspect printed forms rendered as “儿(貌)” in the OCR, whereas the scan appears to show an uncommon character; that unrelated occurrence is left outside this 菜 evidence and was not transcribed or proposed for repair.
